rationale: Both refactors replace the confusing character-by-character state machine with the same clean, line-oriented design: emphasis first, then each line handled as a header, list item or paragraph, using strings.Builder. A splits the work into many small, well-named helpers, which reads nicely. However, it calls headerLevel twice per header line and isListItem twice per line, and it accepts any line starting with '*' (even without a space) as a list item. B's headerLevel returns (level, ok), checks bounds and requires a following space, so it recognises headers more precisely and is more robust. B's list check uses the stricter '* ' prefix. Its control flow, with an early continue for list items, is compact and easy to follow, and its refactoring notes are clearer and more detailed. B is a little more robust and avoids redundant work without giving up readability.
